verdict.pair_reasons: X vs Y: Y wins. Y states M5 (ENGAGE_VERIFY=1 gate — recycle/dry fires never open a row, :509/:10662/:13215), all four M6 stale cross-file citations, and both M7 stale pane-capture citations; X states none of M5/M7, none of M6(a-c), and affirmatively says wrap-ledger's session-continue.sh:608-612 citation 'held' when it does not. X also inverts the wake-floor goal-abstain condition (:697 requires pend>0, X says 'no pending mail') and omits the landed_ok condition on cloud-return's return path (K8). Y's defects are line-number slips (:3230 for the goal call, deathwatch :42/:62/:36-37), none of which change a substantive claim. X vs Z: Z wins. Z has M5 and K8's landed_ok condition, plus verified extras (torn-line `[ inputs ]` behaviour with its three per-reader fallbacks, goal arm not gated on NB_ARMED_TARGET, dry-run discharge defect); X has the inverted goal-abstain claim and the false '608-612 held' assertion. Z's one material overclaim (stamp only on rc 0 — refuted by mark_fired_peer at :10936) is narrower than X's two wrong statements. Y vs Z: Y wins narrowly. Both hit every K item and M1-M5; the verified difference is the brief's explicit citation-check demand: Y catches all of M6 (8936, 7100, 7087, 608-612), both halves of M7 (:302 and :197), the :3520 and :3557 stale cites, and refutes cloud-retire-terminal:180's 'refuses a second discharge' mechanism against cc-custody:229-233; Z covers only 7087, 1058→302 and :3520, and carries one wrong claim (rc-1 rows can only reach self-close via the :8390 repair, refuted by :10936). Z's torn-line and goal-arm insights are real and verified, but Y's cloud-ping-cannot-discharge finding (cloud/<id> matches neither marker nor slug) is of equal weight, leaving Y's fuller citation audit and Z's wrong claim as the deciding difference.
